key_insight: DFT screening predicts that Ag, Ge, and Cd additions can enhance vacancy-mediated transport in bcc Li enough to reach a critical current density of 1 mA cm⁻² within their solubility limits.
engineering_relevance: Vacancy-enhanced Li solid-solution anodes could reduce stripping-induced interfacial void formation and enable higher-current solid-state batteries.
method: Screen 50 substitutional solutes using DFT phase diagrams, solution energies, vacancy binding, and experimental solubility limits.
Estimate critical current density with a dilute-limit adaptation of the Lomer model.
Assess migration barriers and train machine-learning models to reject unsuitable solutes early.
evidence_signal: The thermodynamic model predicts approximately 4 mA cm⁻² for Li–Ag at approximately 9 at.% Ag, with a theoretical capacity of 1522 mAh g⁻¹.
watch_item: Vacancy trapping may partially offset the predicted enhancement; molecular dynamics validation is still needed.
paper_title: Vacancy-enhanced Li solid-solution anodes for solid-state batteries: computational screening enabling high critical current density
